title: Spiced Lamb Flatbread
subtitle: Turkish lahmacun with lamb mince, cumin, allspice, and parsley
excerpt: Lahmacun is a thin, crisp Turkish flatbread spread with a spiced lamb mince topping and baked at very high heat. The dough is simple and quick to make, and the lamb topping takes just minutes to prepare. Roll them up with fresh salad and a squeeze of lemon to serve.
sourceNotes: Based on the Turkish flatbread lahmacun. The spice mix of cumin, allspice, and cinnamon with grated onion follows the traditional Gaziantep preparation.

content.text: Spread the lamb topping as thinly as possible right to the edges of the dough. A thick layer will not cook through properly and the flatbread will stay doughy underneath it.
Make the dough. Mix the bread flour with 4g fast-action yeast, half a tsp of salt, the olive oil, and 180ml warm water. Knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and leave to rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the lamb mince with the grated onion, garlic, tomato puree, cumin, allspice, cinnamon, chilli flakes, and parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well with your hands until fully combined.
Heat the oven to 230C. Place two baking trays in the oven to heat up. Divide the dough into 4 pieces. Roll each piece out very thinly, about 2 to 3mm, into a rough oval or rectangle.

Spread a quarter of the lamb mixture very thinly over each flatbread, right to the edges. Slide onto the hot baking trays. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the edges are crisp and the lamb is cooked through.
Serve immediately. Roll up with fresh salad, sliced cucumber, and a squeeze of lemon.

items.symptom: Dough tears when rolling very thin.
items.fix: Rest for 5 more minutes before rolling again.

items.symptom: Lamb topping is pale and steamed.
items.cause: Spread too thickly or tray not preheated.
items.fix: Spread more thinly and use a hotter, pre-heated tray.
Preheat the tray in the oven for longer next time.
